doc.title: Helen Oakley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

title: Meeting Stanley Dance, their long romance and marriage
summary: She met Stanley in 1936-37, wrote for ten years, and her mother's call led to their marriage.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Now you met Stanley at first in ‘37 was it?
‘36 when I was recording and he came to the sessions. ‘37. I knew he’d correct me on the dates because I never —
So you had a ten year romance?
I mean you’ve had a lifelong romance, let me rephrase that.

I must tell a story about my mother. Because Stanley very bravely and wonderfully, well as Webb said, “Okay that boy’s in love wich you.” And so Stan made a trip over after the war you see? We’d been writing once a year for ten years. That’s all we’d do. But my family and his family, who were lovely, they were terribly good to mine. My brother, who died over there, he was his best man when he was married and they were great

friends, and my sister, who did die later, was a Captain in the Canadian Army, and was the first woman to step into Rome after it fell. She was quite a wonderful person. And so I joined the U.S. Army and my mother said to me, “I don’t understand you” she said, “What about the British lion?” I said, “Well there’s always the American eagle.” She didn’t like it. The British lion you see, if you were in the Canadian Army. But anyway, so when Stanley came over, she telephoned one night from Toronto and said, “Well, what’s it all about? I mean what’s it going to come to?” And that’s when I knew I would marry Stanley because she said to Stanley, “What’s the story?” And Stanley said, “Well, she only loves me on Tuesdays and Thursdays.” And I thought I certainly will marry that man. And so we went up to Toronto and everything was very wonderful you see.
Did you get married on a Tuesday or a Thursday?
Did we. But he took me to England and it was lovely you know. And we had our 51st wedding anniversary this year.
